texts.preamble: Shri P. Selvaraj & Ors vs The Union Of India & Ors on 4 October, 2016 Author: Dipankar Datta Bench: Dipankar Datta
texts.facts: An order dated 21.09.2016 issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Andaman and Nicobar Islands (hereafter the commissioner) is under challenge in this writ petition. Invoking the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereafter the 2006 Act) read with the regulations framed thereunder, the commissioner prohibited "the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of all forms of processed/flavoured/scented chewing tobacco, whether going by the name or form of Gutka, Pan Masala, Zarda packed and unpacked/loose, tobacco leaf in any form etc; and pan masala based sugar boiled based confectioneries in the entire Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands for a period of one year from 2nd October, 2016 in the interest of public health."
texts.arguments: Mr. Dutta, learned senior advocate representing the petitioners has contended as follows: 1. The 2006 Act does not apply to tobacco and tobacco products and, therefore, invocation of provisions thereof is illegal and absolutely unauthorized. According to him, the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Shri P. Selvaraj & Ors vs The Union Of India & Ors on 4 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56200172/ 1 Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (hereafter the 2003 Act) is the relevant enactment that could have been invoked, for, it empowers total prohibition of sale of cigarettes and other tobacco products; 2. Mr. Dutta next cited the judgment and order dated 19.07.2016 of a Division Bench of the Patna High Court in CWJC 3805 of 2015 (M/s. Omkar Agency Vs. The State of Bihar & Anr.) According to him, since a High Court in the country has [LEAKAGE_MASK] a similar order, having regard to the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the decisions reported in (2004) 6 SCC 254 (Kusum Ingots & Alloys Ltd. Vs. Union of India) and (2008) 14 SCC 283 (Pradip J. Mehta Vs. Commissioner of Income Tax, Ahmedabad), the petitioners are entitled to an interim order of stay of operation of the impugned order; and 3. Food is defined in section 3(j) of the 2006 Act as follows: (j) "food" means any substance, whether processed, partially processed or unprocessed, which is intended for human consumption and includes......................." Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety And Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011 provides that "tobacco and nicotine shall not be used as ingredients in any food products". For facility of reference, section 6 of the 2003 Act is quoted below: "6. Prohibition on sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to a person below the age of eighteen years and in particular area. - No person shall sell, offer for sale, or permit sale of, cigarette or any other tobacco product - (a) to any person who is under eighteen years of age, and (b) in an area within a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution." In the considered prima facie view of this Bench, "and" between clauses (a) and (b) ought to be read as "or"; or else, sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to persons under eighteen years of age could be transacted at an area just beyond a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution. The Division Bench decision of the Patna High Court in M/s.
